neighbours.label: grains and cereals as a food group (whole grains, wheat, flour, oats)
fire: A healthy plate includes plenty of vegetables and whole grains such as brown rice.
For breakfast, try a bowl of porridge made from rolled oats.
The bread is baked with stone-ground wheat from a local mill.
Most of the fibre in her diet comes from barley and rye.
Swap white pasta for whole grain versions to feel full for longer.
Fortified breakfast cereals are a common source of iron for children.
The farmers harvest the wheat in late summer and store it in silos.
Mix the flour with a pinch of salt before adding the water.
quiet: A healthy plate includes plenty of vegetables and lean fish such as salmon.
For breakfast, try a bowl of yogurt topped with fresh berries.
The soup is made with tomatoes picked from a local garden.
Most of the vitamin C in her diet comes from oranges and peppers.
Swap fried chicken for grilled versions to cut down on fat.
Fortified milk is a common source of vitamin D for children.
The farmers pick the apples in late summer and store them in barns.
Mix the eggs with a pinch of salt before adding the butter.

notes: Card: ' grains' x8, wheat, grass, Arabic wheat/flour; output promotes wheat, flour, bread, cereal. The - pole is protein/meat and chopping. Near misses are the same diet-advice frame with other food groups.
